title: When It Comes to End-Users and Customers, It's All About Reducing Friction
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case that sustainable competitive advantage depends less on having a superior product and more on relentlessly reducing the friction customers experience using it. The author defines friction broadly, as anything that makes it harder for end-users to realize the full value of a product, and breaks it into specific categories: discovery, sign-up, usability, support, and scalability friction. Great organizations continuously observe how customers actually experience their offering and systematically eliminate obstacles in each of these areas, since even loyal customers will eventually leave for a lower-friction alternative.
points: Reducing friction, not just improving the product, is essential to sustained competitive advantage.
Friction is defined as anything that blocks end-users from realizing the full value of a product or service.
The article breaks friction into five categories: discovery, sign-up, usability, support, and scalability.
Even loyal customers will eventually leave for a lower-friction alternative if friction persists.
Speaking with and observing end-users directly is key to finding hidden sources of friction.
quotes: To achieve and sustain a competitive advantage in any marketplace, leaders must relentlessly reduce the friction end-users and customers experience with their products and services.
Friction refers to anything that makes it more difficult for end-users to realize the full value and benefit of a product or service.
Great organizations continually examine how end-users experience their product or service and identify every point of friction that exists.
Discovery friction includes any struggle about how to navigate or use the product or service.
Anything that chafes is a barrier to adoption and must be stamped out.
Eliminating friction is a never-ending job that pays big dividends in customer growth and loyalty.
